name: Block Dominoes with Spinners
description: Block Dominoes with Spinners is a variant of Block Dominoes where the first double played becomes a 'spinner' â€” tiles can be placed on all four sides of it, creating a cross-shaped layout with up to four open ends. This dramatically increases the number of playable positions compared to the two-end standard block game. The key question is whether ONLY the first double is a spinner, or ALL doubles are spinners.

overview.description: Block Dominoes with Spinners is a variant of Block Dominoes where the first double played becomes a 'spinner' â€” tiles can be placed on all four sides of it, creating a cross-shaped layout with up to four open ends. This dramatically increases the number of playable positions compared to the two-end standard block game. The key question is whether ONLY the first double is a spinner, or ALL doubles are spinners.

history.origins: A modification of standard Block Dominoes that adds the 'spinner' mechanic â€” allowing play on all four sides of a double. This creates the cross-shaped layouts familiar from many American domino games.
timeline: Traditional: Evolved from standard Block Dominoes as players sought more dynamic layouts.
19th-20th century: Spinner mechanic becomes standard in many American and Dutch domino traditions.
Present: One of the most common domino variants globally.
history.cultural: The spinner mechanic is so dominant in American domino play that many Americans don't even know non-spinner variants exist. The 'chicken foot' layout style (angling tiles away from the spinner centre) reflects the practical table-space challenges of multi-spinner games.
history.evolution: The spinner mechanic transforms the simple two-end block game into a multi-branch puzzle. American domino culture strongly favours spinners, while British and many European traditions play without them.

setup.players: 2 to 4 players. Partnership play possible with 4.
setup.deck: Double-six domino set (28 tiles). Can also use double-nine or double-twelve sets for more players.
setup.dealing: 2 players: 7 tiles each. 3 players: 5 tiles each. 4 players: 5 tiles each. Remaining tiles stay in the boneyard.
setup.equipment: Double-six domino set. Optional: Cribbage board for scoring.

rules.objective: Be the first to play all your tiles, or have the fewest pips when the game blocks.
rules.gameplay: On your turn, match a tile to any open end of the layout. The spinner (first double played) allows play on all four sides, creating up to four open arms. If you can't play, you pass.
keyRules: The first double played is ALWAYS a spinner (playable on all 4 sides).
Must fill both long sides of the spinner before playing on the short sides.
Subsequent doubles: either crosswise-only (common) or also spinners (all-spinner variant).
No drawing from boneyard â€” pass if you can't play (block mechanic).
Layout can become complex with multiple branches.

strategy.basic: Lead with your strongest suit. Spinners open up more ends, giving you more options â€” control which numbers appear on the open ends.
strategy.intermediate: With the spinner creating 4 open ends, suit diversity is more valuable than in standard block. Track which numbers are on the open ends and which are depleted.
strategy.advanced: In partnerships, communicate through play: your lead signals your strong suit. With all-spinners variant, the layout becomes extremely open â€” the game becomes more about hand management than blocking. In the single-spinner variant, controlling the spinner's four arms is the key strategic battleground.
tips: Control the spinner arms â€” they're the most flexible play positions.
With 4 open ends, you're less likely to be blocked, so focus on emptying your hand efficiently.
In all-spinners variant, the game becomes very open â€” high-pip tiles become liabilities.
Larger sets (double-nine, double-twelve) with spinners can create 8-arm layouts.

variations.name: Single Spinner
variations.description: Only the first double is a spinner. Other doubles are placed crosswise but not expanded. The more strategic variant.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant only changes how many doubles act as spinners; no numeric engine constants differ.

variations.name: All Spinners
variations.description: Every double is a spinner â€” creates extremely branching layouts. Less strategic due to many open ends. Can require 'chicken foot' placement to fit on the table.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: All-spinners play uses the same scoring and deal sizes; differences are layout structure, not numeric constants.

variations.name: Dutch Variant (with Draw)
variations.description: When unable to play, draw 1-2 tiles from boneyard. Last two tiles remain undrawn. Double-zero counts as 13 pips.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Dutch draw rules adjust drawing and scoring details; the engine model does not yet expose separate tunable constants.

variations.name: Double-Nine Eight-Arm
variations.description: With double-nine set, play starts on all four sides AND four corners of the spinner, giving 8 arms.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Eight-arm play from double-nine mainly affects layout geometry; no separate engine override fields have been modeled.

scoring.description: Winner scores losers' pips minus own pips. Game to 101 (2p) or 61 (3-4p).
scoring.winCondition: First to target score across multiple rounds.

synthesis.shortDescription: Block Dominoes with a cross-shaped twist. The first double becomes a 'spinner' â€” playable on all four sides. This creates 4 open ends instead of 2, dramatically increasing options. Some play with all doubles as spinners, creating wild branching layouts.
